text: Marta Rivera: Heads-up — Big customer asked for parity with CompetitorX's "new streaming-embeddings" feature. They're saying it would cut their inference latency by 40% and unblock a pilot. Need triage.
thread:
LaunchBot: incident-bot: signal detected: competitor feature launched (CompetitorX v2) 

Kevin Chu: can you paste the ask / customer details? small wins vs full parity matters here

Marta Rivera: @Kevin Chu — customer ACME, pilot next quarter. They called out streaming embeddings + per-request prefetch. Short ask: match latency profile, not necessarily identical API.

Priya Nair: quick thought — we have the infra pieces: prefix caching + continuous batching in runtime. Main gaps are emb streaming API surface + kv prefetching on client side.

Ethan Cole: options: 
- A) ship a compatibility shim: surface-level API + server-side stream proxy -> ~2 sprints
- B) invest in native streaming embeddings with prefetch + backpressure -> ~6-8 wks, better unit economics
Which do we prefer?

Kevin Chu: +1 to documenting options. We should validate business impact: will this win the deal or just be nice-to-have? Also check infra load estimates.

Marta Rivera: ACME says it's blocking their go/no-go. So it's deal-impacting. That nudges us toward A unless we can accelerate B with a spike.

Priya Nair: proposal: 1-week spike to prototype shim and measure perf; 2-week parallel design for native approach. OK to scope spike to minimal API surface + load test with sample traces.

Ethan Cole: agree. Success criteria for spike: prototype can stream tokens with <=2x CPU overhead vs current embedding requests and show end-to-end latency within 20% of CompetitorX numbers.

Kevin Chu: risks: compatibility maintenance, SDK churn, and routing complexity (dedicated vs hosted). If we do shim, add feature flag + automatic fallback.

Marta Rivera: owners: @Priya leads spike, @Ethan for infra perf, @Kevin for API/SDK compatibility. I'll own customer comms and update ACME by EOD Friday.

Priya Nair: started a doc: https://go.redwood/docs/product/streams-parity-spike (internal). I put initial acceptance criteria and test vectors.

LaunchBot: deploy-bot: spike branch created (refs/heads/spike/streaming-shim). CI started.

Ethan Cole: quick note on prioritization: if spike shows low effort/high impact, we'll carve this into next sprint and shift one lower-priority story (probably "small-model-routing-refactor").

Kevin Chu: ship/rollback plan: feature-flagged rollout to hosted first, gather telemetry for two weeks, then flip for Dedicated customers on request.

Marta Rivera: decision summary: run 1-week prototype spike + 2-week design parallel. If prototype passes perf gates, schedule parity shim for next sprint and keep native streaming as medium-term roadmap bet. I'll update roadmap doc and flag for PM review.
